title: LCP binding profile (§8.3 / §8.3.1)
$comment: A named binding-profile document — the serialized BindingManifest a rail publishes. `pattern` is pinned to the §8.3 seven-name enum: this is the TYPE-LEVEL catch for the misclassification (x402 nonce=atrHash was archived as `id-reuse` by reading MPP-EVM's Appendix-C.1 derivation-MUST onto a path that has no derivation; ruled off-canonical Native Field per §8.3.1/B.1 on 2026-07-16). `nativeField` is present iff `pattern` is `native-field`.

rail.description: The settlement rail this profile binds (evm:x402 | evm:escrow | solana | …).

protocol.description: OPTIONAL — the commerce protocol this binding is specific to, and never required. Absent iff the binding is protocol-neutral: evm:escrow is a MECHANISM several protocols settle through, and the bare-rail bindings bind no protocol at all, so absence is the correct state for 8 of the 12 shipped profiles. `rail` above stays the scheme id; the two are different fields with different jobs. The enum is INLINED from vocabulary/protocol-id.schema.json rather than $ref'd — the runner passes schemas inline and the subject's validator has no file resolver for a relative external ref — and a package test guards this copy against that file.

pattern.description: The LCP §8.3 binding-pattern name — load-bearing; an unknown value is rejected here, not silently accepted as prose.

nativeField.description: The existing protocol field carrying the binding value — present iff pattern = native-field.

assetBinding.description: Whether — and how — the recovery path observes the settled asset. filtered: recovery reads the token's own log, so the record proves THIS token moved. carried: the token's identity is written into the record itself. proposal-only: the asset is named when the payment is proposed but never re-checked at recovery. none: recovery never observes the asset — the weld rides the transaction envelope, which is indifferent to its payload (the same property that makes the rail asset-independent). Four values because measurement found four cases (2026-08-03); a boolean cannot express proposal-only honestly. The zeroPartyRecoverable precedent governs: a weaker evidentiary claim is DECLARED as weaker, never enforced away — recorder, not judge.

successGate.description: HOW the recovery path knows the settlement actually happened — the sibling axis to assetBinding (that one declares whether recovery observes WHAT moved; this declares whether it observes THAT anything moved). raw-field: the rail RECORDS failed transactions along with their weld payload, so the reader supplies the chain's own outcome field and recovery gates on it, fail-closed — absent is never evidence of success. structural: the rail cannot produce a failed transaction that still carries a weld (a reverted EVM tx emits no logs, an aborted Sui PTB discards its events, a Daml command that did not commit leaves no contract), so no field is read; the claim is about the rail and is only as durable as the reader's data source. Deliberately NO third value — 'recovery cannot tell' is not a posture a profile may publish, it is the defect the 2026-08-03 success-gate sweep closed on stellar and cardano. Unlike assetBinding's 'none', which is an honest declaration that a rail does not observe the asset, no rail may legitimately not observe settlement and still claim to record one.

indexing.description: How settlements are forward-indexed to the atrHash (nonce-topic:… | event-data-scan:… | …).

finality.description: PAY-3/RCS-5 finality declaration — finality is never represented as dispute resolution.

weldGrades.description: Per-collection-path weld grade — signature-grade (the payer's signature commits the binding) or tx-grade.

offCanonical.description: §8.3.1 off-canonical Native Field variant reference (the named-profile name, not a hedge).

lifecycleStates.description: The lifecycle state set for this binding.

allOf.$comment: a non-native pattern MUST NOT carry nativeField — the iff's other direction.
